A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFI/PepMirror research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original latent-space analyses, LNR benchmark experiments, and CD38 binding assays for generated D-peptides.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds reflection tests, model-variant evaluations, and experimental enantiomer controls.

M1.justification: Appendix A.7 adds variants combining all three axial features, injecting pseudoscalars directly into node features, and injecting them only once after GNN initialization. The original AFI-EPT architecture, latent diffusion framework, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: PepBench, ProtFrag, LNR, and CD38 remain the underlying datasets and target. Coverage expands to six reflected-pocket input scenarios and wet-lab testing of L-1412, the opposite enantiomer of D-1412 (Appendices A.1 and A.6).

E2.justification: The external baseline roster is unchanged. However, the corresponding Rosetta comparison adds PepMirror(scalar) alongside the existing methods and variants (v1 Table S5; v2 Table S7).

E3.justification: New protocols test reflections across three coordinate planes and three randomly sampled planes, compare original/inverted/reflected pocket representations, and introduce enantiomer binding and circular-dichroism controls. Existing splits, 100 designs per LNR target, evaluation metrics, and listed training epochs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands supplementary validation: reflection robustness and latent equivalence tests (Tables S1–S2), mixed/scalar/single-injection ablations (Tables S8–S9), and L-enantiomer binding plus circular-dichroism controls (Appendix A.6, Figure S8). These address symmetry implementation, dependence on feature-injection choices, and stereoselectivity of the principal experimental binder.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 newly states that BLI assays were repeated to validate binding by both enantiomers, but provides no repetition count. Existing seed information and D-1412 affinity estimates of 9.9 ± 0.2 and 10.5 ± 0.6 micromolar are unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds reflection and latent-distance results, mixed/scalar variant scores, and the consequential finding that L-1412 binds CD38 with affinity comparable to D-1412. Table S9 additionally reports raw D-chirality of 99.33% for triple_scalar versus 97.05% for triple_scalar_once. Tables 1–2 and all pre-existing diversity and Rosetta result rows remain unchanged; these additions are not performance gains for the original models.

T1.justification: New Lemma B.11 and its proof extend the inversion-discrepancy result to arbitrary improper orthogonal transformations. Equation (31) also gains a minus sign in the commutator identity. The existing chirality-separation and diffusion-stability arguments are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The conclusion broadens AFI's contribution framing toward a general chirality-injection principle, including pseudoscalar implementations beyond vector-channel injection. The central cross-chirality generalization, benchmark superiority, and first wet-lab-validated generative D-peptide design claims remain.

C2.justification: V1 emphasizes modeled interactions depending on correct stereochemistry. V2 retains that statement but materially qualifies the wet-lab interpretation by acknowledging comparable binding of both enantiomers and discussing flexibility or alternative binding modes. It also newly attributes random-plane representation deviations to PDB coordinate rounding and discusses broader applicability of scalar injection.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-repository pointer. Conversely, v2 Table S10 omits the learning-rate decay factor of 0.8 and five-epoch scheduler patience documented in v1 Table S6. This establishes a documentation loss, without establishing that the training schedule changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Newcombe et al. (2024) and Li et al. (2026) to contextualize limited stereoselectivity. It replaces the Tetra-DMPNN attribution to Du et al. (2024) with Pattanaik et al. (2020), and removes the ChiralCliff discussion and Schneider et al. (2018) citation.

P1.justification: Changes include targeted expansions of the wet-lab discussion and conclusion, new appendix subsections, clarified triple-product terminology, updated affiliations, and acknowledgements. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds four supplementary tables and the circular-dichroism plot in Figure S8, extends the Rosetta table, and shortens the hyperparameter table. Figure 1 moves earlier, Figure 5 gains a KD annotation, and running headers and page flow change. Existing visualizations are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The reflection proof/tests, additional ablations, and enantiomer/CD controls strengthen validation and make the biological interpretation more informative. The improvement is limited by qualitative-only reporting of L-1412 affinity, unspecified BLI repetition counts, and removal of scheduler details. The principal quantitative evidence remains intact, supporting a modest net improvement.
